_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Accounting P2 (Managerial Accounting and Managing Resources), November 2019 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The optional
'information' field (array of lines) carries the INFORMATION block of each main question; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that main question and applies to all of its sub-questions.
The pre-printed ANSWER BOOK (paper2_answer_book.pdf) is tracked beside the paper.
memo_answer reproduces the marking guideline's figures and workings line by line (tick marks
removed; marking notes such as 'one part correct' kept). Unnumbered bullet sub-parts of a
question are kept in one entry with their marks added.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Cost Accounting and Internal Control 45 marks 36 min; Q2 Inventory
and VAT 25 marks 20 min; Q3 Budgets 35 marks 28 min; Q4 Reconciliations, Fixed Assets, Ratio Analysis
and Internal Control 45 marks 36 min; total 150 marks, 2 hours. A Grade 10 formula sheet (Annexure A)
is attached to the paper (not transcribed here). The marking guideline numbers the answer to 1.2.2
as a second '1.2.1'. In 2.2 (headed INVENTORY in the paper, ACCOUNTING EQUATION in the guideline) the
learner completes the blank cells of the table; memo_answer gives the completed rows.

questions.context: QUESTION 1: COST ACCOUNTING AND INTERNAL CONTROL (45 marks; 36 minutes) | 1.1 Answer the following questions.
questions.text: Direct material cost plus direct labour cost is equal to …
Differentiate between a trading business and a manufacturing business.
questions.memo_answer:
• A trading business buys and sells goods to the public to make a profit.
• A manufacturing business buys raw materials, converts/manufactures it to finished goods and sells to retailers or directly to the public.

questions.text: Define fixed cost and a variable cost and give ONE example of each cost.
questions.memo_answer:
• Fixed cost remains the same no matter how many units are produced, e.g. rent expense, Insurance, salaries, etc.
• Variable cost changes with the number of units produced e.g. raw materials direct labour, advertising, water and electricity, etc.

questions.context: 1.2 Lynx Sportswear is a small business that manufactures football jerseys which are supplied to the local schools. During June 2019 the business manufactured 7 460 jerseys.
information: Fabric (material) used in the production of jerseys R180 000
Rent expense total (60% allocated to factory) 16 200
Water and electricity (2/3 allocated to factory) 9 600
questions.text: Calculate the following: • Direct material cost (3) • Direct labour cost (2) • Factory / manufacturing overheads (8) • Total cost of production (5) • Unit cost per jersey (4)
questions.memo_answer:
Direct material cost: 180 000 + 32 500 = 212 500
Direct labour cost: 210 000
Factory / manufacturing overhead cost: 18 700 + (16 200 x 60%) + (9 600 x 2/3) + 5 200 = 40 020 (one part correct)
OR 18 700 (1 mark) + 9 720 (2 marks) + 6 400 (2 marks) + 5 200 (1 mark)
Total cost of production: 212 500 + 210 000 + 40 020 = 462 520 (one part correct)
Unit cost per jersey: 462 520 / 7 460 = R62 (one part correct)

questions.text: The accountant is concerned that the sales for the year dropped by 40% and the cost of sales was higher than the previous year. This was due to an increase in the wool price and also transport cost. (a) Suggest THREE strategies to achieve the objective of increasing profits. (6) (b) If the sales for last year were R500 000 and the profit mark-up is 25%, calculate: • The sales for the current year (5) • The cost of sales for the current year (5)
questions.memo_answer:
(a) THREE valid responses:
• Look for cheaper suppliers
• Extend the target market
• Use local suppliers
• Reduce overtime
• Retrenchment (as a last resort)
(b) Sales for the current year: 60% x 500 000 = 300 000 (one part correct)
Cost of sales for the current year: 100/125 x 300 000 = 240 000 (one part correct)

questions.context: QUESTION 3: BUDGETS (35 marks; 28 minutes) | Kamva High School from East London has decided to go on an educational field tour to Port Elizabeth. The tour group will consist of two educators and ten learners. They have asked you to do some calculations of various costs for the tour so that they can do proper planning and budgeting to ensure that the tour is a success. Further information supplied: • Transport with school bus from East London to Port Elizabeth is R450 per learner. (The teachers do not pay for transport.) • Accommodation in Port Elizabeth is R300 per room per night and two learners will share a room while the teachers will have single rooms each at a cost of R250 per room. They will book for ONE night. • The VW factory tour is free of charge. They will visit the museum and snake park that has an entry fee of R20 per person; however a school group gets a 10% discount. • They are budgeting a total of R120 per person for meals. NOTE: The school will pay for the teachers' accommodation and meals. | 3.1 Calculate the following:
questions.text: Total transport costs for the learners
Cost of accommodation for the learners
Cost of accommodation for the teachers
questions.memo_answer: 2 rooms x R250 = R500 (one part correct)

questions.text: Total cost of accommodation for the teachers and the learners
Cost for the tour group for the visit to the museum and snake park
questions.memo_answer:
(12 persons x 20) less 10% discount
240 - 24 = R216 (one part correct)

questions.text: Total cost for all the meals for the group
questions.memo_answer:
12 persons x 120 = R1 440 (one part correct)
(Teachers 240 + learners 1 200)

questions.text: TOTAL cost for the tour
questions.memo_answer:
Transport + accommodation + visits + meals = total costs
4 500 + 1 500 + 500 + 216 + 1 440 = R8 156 (one part correct)

questions.text: Cost per learner for the tour

questions.context: 3.2 Sindi Mpoma, the school clerk, has been approached by the teachers to organise the trip for them. She will make the bookings for teachers and the learners. Sindi thought of asking for a discount for learners from the hotel where they have booked and to use the extra money to book her holiday trip of two days in December with her family. She decided not to tell anyone about her plans.
questions.text: Should Sindi go ahead with her plan? Motivate your answer.
questions.memo_answer: No. This is unethical. Negotiating a discount for learners and concealing the information from them with the hope of using it for personal gain is a criminal offence.

questions.text: What consequences could Sindi face should she decide to go ahead with the plan and is caught? Give ONE point.
questions.memo_answer:
• She could be charged with fraud
• She could be suspended from work
• She would have to pay back the money
Any reasonable answer

questions.context: 4.3 RATIO ANALYSIS. Pambo Stores is a clothing store that sells cheap imported clothes manufactured in China. Their mark-up on cost price is 75%. Use the given information to answer the questions that follow.
information: PAMBO STORES - EXTRACT FROM INCOME STATEMENT FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 JUNE 2019
Financial indicators for the year ended 30 June 2018:
questions.text: Calculate the percentage Gross profit on sales for 2019. Compare results with 2018. Quote figures and comment.
questions.memo_answer:
480 000 / 1 280 000 x 100 = 37,5% (one part correct)
Decreased by 4,4%: GP % on sales decreased from 41,9% in 2018 to 37,5% in 2019. Sales have increased, but the increase in cost of sales may have resulted in this decrease.

questions.text: Calculate the percentage Operating expenses on sales for 2019. Compare with 2018. Quote figures and comment.
questions.memo_answer:
118 800 / 1 280 000 x 100 = 9,3% (one part correct)
Decreased slightly by 0,2%: decreased from 9,5% in 2018 to 9,3% in 2019. Increase in sales may have resulted in the small decrease.

questions.text: Calculate the percentage Net profit on sales for 2019. Compare with 2018. Quote figures and comment.
questions.memo_answer:
389 550 / 1 280 000 x 100 = 30,4% (one part correct)
Decreased by 4,7%: % net profit on sales decreased from 35,1% in 2018 to 30,4% in 2019. This may be due to increase in expenses in 2019.
